findings.obligation: Every rule that sees a moved platform type today still sees it after the move; the oracle law must reflect how consumers match
findings.observation: Alternatives are per-type full-name regexes, e.g. ^Lighthouse\.Backend\.Platform\.(UpdateQueue\.(AdmittedCancellations|...|UpdateTaskNaming))(\.|$). Consumers match NAMESPACES (IlDependencies.cs:44-48 Regex.IsMatch(NamespaceOf(type), pattern); ArchUnit ResideInNamespaceMatching). Namespace Lighthouse.Backend.Platform.UpdateQueue has no trailing type name so the alternative never matches; after feature B moves the types, TheKeyRing, TheUpdateQueue, TheUpdateCode, TheUpdateComponents, PortfolioDeliveryPattern, ServicesImplementationPattern, AnImplementationNamespace, PromisesAndTheUpdateCode and WorkItemsPolicies patterns stop seeing them. Oracle evaluates full type names so it is green 8/8 while the promise fails in substance.
findings.remediation: Design decision: (a) consumers match full type names (change IlDependencies and ArchUnit predicates) so per-type alternatives work, or (b) widen by Platform area namespace and accept rules seeing more types, amending the preservation law; then the oracle must evaluate namespaces as consumers do and the crafter realigns.
